newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE jails copyright violator in landmark sentence.
newsitem.headline: UAE jails copyright violator in landmark sentence.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates has for the first time sentenced a copyright violator to prison after convicting him of selling pirated video cassettes, the Motion Picture Association (MPA) said.

The 31-year-old Indian man was sentenced to a month in jail after raids on his video store and a duplication site early this year uncovered 370 illegal video cassettes, the MPA said in a statement received on Sunday.
"This should serve as a very serious warning to everyone involved in piracy," MPA Middle East General Manager Scott Butler said.

"(The case) highlights the fact that the courts are handing out harsher sentences and we firmly believe that this trend will continue," said Essam al-Tamimi, managing partner at the law firm Al-Tamimi and Co which represents the MPA in the UAE.
The firm also filed a civil suit against the offender, reserving the right to sue for loss and damages in the future.
The UAE introduced copyright laws in 1992 as part of efforts to make the country more attractive to foreign investors.
In recent years, authorities have stepped up the drive to enforce the law and regularly raided shops and companies suspected of selling pirated goods, a widespread practice in the oil-rich Gulf.
